title: Most children walk up a few stairs by about two years, CDC says
summary: CDC says most children, 75 percent or more, walk up a few stairs, not by climbing them, by about two years.
body: On the 2-year milestone page, CDC lists walks, not climbs, up a few stairs with or without help. The heading is what most children do by that age, and the program defines a milestone as something 75 percent or more of children can do. The materials are not a substitute for a validated screening tool, and a missed stair skill is not itself a diagnosis. The page tells families to raise concerns with a clinician rather than wait them out. Stair gates are a separate product card. This card is only the timing CDC prints.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Years
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Reviewed 16 May 2026. Milestone means most children (75 percent or more), not every child, and the page says the materials are not a screening tool.
